summary: The Middle Kingdom from the gilded peace of 4A 1748 through the Golden King's death, the four-camp succession, the War of the Last Crowns and Eindil's coronation (140 focuses, branches A to N).

offices_for_sale.name: Offices for Sale
offices_for_sale.desc: Anything in the realm with a seal on it can be bought, and the buyers expect to be repaid.

gilded_parim.name: Gilded Parim
gilded_parim.desc: Gold leaf glitters on every pillar of the capital. The city has never looked richer, and the people have never felt more pleased with their King.

merchant_houses.name: The Merchant Houses
merchant_houses.desc: The great trading houses of the lake keep their own agents at court and their own wharves in every port.

honest_accounts.name: Honest Accounts
honest_accounts.desc: Every sum that enters or leaves the treasury is written in an open ledger. It is slow, and it is clean.

royal_auditors.name: The Royal Auditors
royal_auditors.desc: Auditors in grey robes walk the offices of the realm with their rods and their ink. Clerks have learned to check their sums twice.

jubilee_celebrations.name: The Golden Jubilee
jubilee_celebrations.desc: Bonfires, banquets and bell-ringing for the long reign. For a season the whole realm is at festival.

fleet_of_the_lake.name: The Lake Fleet
fleet_of_the_lake.desc: Broad-beamed galleys patrol the lake in long lines, drilled in oar-signals and fire-pot drill.

sea_routes.name: Trade Across the Sea
sea_routes.desc: Aenoran cogs call at harbours from the Ocean of Peace to the western isles, and foreign merchants know the lake colours.

learned_halls.name: The Universities
learned_halls.desc: The halls of Parim and Selen share their masters and their books, and learning moves briskly between them.

realm_of_plenty.name: A Kingdom of Plenty
realm_of_plenty.desc: Barns brim and workshops hum. Builders find timber and journeymen where a few years ago they found excuses.

levies_of_the_concord.name: The Concord Levies
levies_of_the_concord.desc: Each dominion keeps its quota of spears on the rolls, drilled by the village reeve and ready on the King's word.

common_army_drill.name: The Common Army
common_army_drill.desc: Spearmen from every dominion learn the same signals and the same songs. A horn in Selen is understood in Kingson.

concord_renewed.name: The Concord Reborn
concord_renewed.desc: The old compact has been spoken again and believed. Lords who once sulked now ride to Parim of their own accord.

league_of_the_king.name: The King's League
league_of_the_king.desc: Banner, oath and gilt mail: the Lost Cause has its own hall, its own colours and a king who loves to preside.

wall_watch.name: Watchers on the Wall
wall_watch.desc: Beacon-keepers and signal-masters sleep in the towers, and their lamps are lit before dusk.

first_light_houses.name: The Houses of the First Light
first_light_houses.desc: Hospitals, granaries and birth rolls, kept by the temples and trusted by the people. Whoever holds the keys holds the realm's gratitude.

temple_scholars.name: The Temple Schools
temple_scholars.desc: The temples teach the young their letters and their prayers in one lesson.

almoners.name: The Royal Almoners
almoners.desc: Bread is handed out at the temple door every dawn, and few ask where the grain comes from.

counted_realm.name: The Birth Rolls
counted_realm.desc: The King now knows how many hands he can call. Recruiting captains no longer need to guess.

crown_blessed.name: The Blessed Crown
crown_blessed.desc: The people kneel to a crown the temples have anointed, and they find it easier to forgive what it does.

blessed_realm.name: One Faith, One Realm
blessed_realm.desc: The Deliverer's rites are kept in every dominion. Dissent is quiet, and so is much else.

own_counsel.name: The King's Own Counsel
own_counsel.desc: The King chooses his councillors himself, and cannot always tell which of them chose him.

bought_commissions.name: Commissions for Sale
bought_commissions.desc: Captains pay for their ranks and expect to recoup the cost. The ranks look splendid and drill poorly.

merit_commissions.name: Commissions by Merit
merit_commissions.desc: Officers rise on trial and record. Noble sons grumble, and the rank and file feel they are worth something.

guard_of_gold.name: The Golden Guard
guard_of_gold.desc: Two thousand picked spears in gilded helms hold the palace gates, and every one of them knows his name is on the roll.

drilled_regiments.name: The Drill Fields
drilled_regiments.desc: Recruits drill on the lakeside meadows from first light under cheerfully merciless drill-masters.

host_of_the_king.name: The King's Host
host_of_the_king.desc: Heavy foot, horse and archers wear the lake colours and march to one horn.

realm_mobilised.name: The Realm Mobilised
realm_mobilised.desc: Beacons burn, bells ring and every village sends its men. Aenor is on a war footing.

kings_awakening.name: The King Awakes
kings_awakening.desc: The King has smelled the poison and understood what it meant. He is sharp, wary and, for the first time in years, truly king.

kings_war.name: The King's War
kings_war.desc: The sovereign is in the field with his own banner. The Host remembers what it is for.

sobered_king.name: A Sobered King
sobered_king.desc: The King has stopped gilding his halls. He listens, he decides and the realm feels the difference.

gold_regency.name: The Regency of Gold
gold_regency.desc: The Golden Court rules in the name of a crown nobody wears. Gold buys loyalty, and the court spends freely.

regency_war_chest.name: The Treasury of War
regency_war_chest.desc: The Regency's hoard has been turned to iron and timber. The forges of the lake never cool.

deliverer_crowned.name: The Deliverer Crowned
deliverer_crowned.desc: The people kneel in the streets as the king passes. Whatever else he is, he is loved.

chancery.name: The Seals of State
chancery.desc: Scribes in white sort the realm's letters, and no decree leaves Parim without the Deliverer's seal.

altar_and_throne.name: Temple and Crown
altar_and_throne.desc: The priests sit beside the throne, and the throne sits within the priests' prayer.

deliverance_shield.name: The Shield of Deliverance
deliverance_shield.desc: Carved wards guard the gates, and the temple guard keeps the towers. Parim feels safe, and will until it learns otherwise.

sworn_realm.name: The Oaths of the Realm
sworn_realm.desc: Every lord has knelt, every captain has sworn. The oaths are kept in a book in the temple vault.

speakers_concord.name: The Speakers' Council
speakers_concord.desc: Each dominion speaks with one voice and one vote. Debates are long, and the decisions are respected.

defence_pact.name: A Common Defence
defence_pact.desc: A shared host under a chosen marshal, and a shared understanding that an attack on one dominion is an attack on all.

concord_stands.name: The Concord Stands
concord_stands.desc: The compact has been remade by consent, and the realm hums with the quiet confidence of a thing that wants to last.

popular_host.name: The Popular Host
popular_host.desc: Rangers, scholars and ploughmen march under one banner. They are poorly equipped and tremendously sure.

glo_light.name: The Light of Glo
glo_light.desc: A green glow in the van of the host. Men say it is hope. The dark things say nothing.

banner_of_the_dragon.name: The Dragon Banner
banner_of_the_dragon.desc: A dragon circles above the host. Horses scream, riders cheer and the foe loses its nerve before the first arrow is shot.

last_alliance.name: The Last Alliance of Men
last_alliance.desc: Banners from the whole of the north and west stand under one king. The host is large, and for once, it is united.

captains_command.name: The Captains' Command
captains_command.desc: The captains hold the keys and give the orders. They are better at the second than the first.

realm_beset.name: Aenor Beset
realm_beset.desc: The realm is attacked on every side. Every wall is manned, every road watched, and every heart a little harder.

lake_levy.name: The Levy of the Lake
lake_levy.desc: One man in three has taken spear and shield. The villages are quiet and the barracks are loud.

common_cause.name: A Common Cause
common_cause.desc: Realms at war with the dark have opened their roads to Aenor, and Aenor has opened hers. Messengers pass freely.

final_stand.name: The Last Stand
final_stand.desc: Every soldier, mason and baker has a post. Nobody asks if the city can be held, because nobody intends to ask what happens if it cannot.

kingdom_of_ruins.name: A Kingdom of Ruins
kingdom_of_ruins.desc: Half the realm is rubble and the other half is scaffolding. Builders are everywhere, and so is dust.

peace_of_treaties.name: Treaties, Not Conquest
peace_of_treaties.desc: The King sends heralds before he sends spears. Neighbours have noticed, and some have begun to answer.

age_of_the_king.name: The Age of the King
age_of_the_king.desc: A new reign in a rebuilt land. The old quarrels are put away, and the realm stands as it has not for centuries.

court_feast.title: A Feast in the Golden Court
court_feast.desc: The steward of the household asks how the high table is to be laid. Three hundred guests will sit before the lamps are lit, and every one of them has sent a gift.

auditors_ledger.title: The Auditors' Ledger
auditors_ledger.desc: The auditors lay their finished ledger before the throne. It lists every gift, bribe and borrowed seal of the last ten years, and it runs to nine volumes.

options.name: Keep it in the royal archive.

caravan_envoys.title: Envoys from Parim
caravan_envoys.desc: Envoys from the Middle Kingdom have crossed the rift sea with silks, glass and the Golden King's greeting. They ask nothing but a place at the caravan masters' feast.

selen_accord.title: An Accord with Parim
selen_accord.desc: A rider in Aenor's gold reaches the green hall of Selen with a scroll under the King's seal. It offers the rangers honour and relief from tolls in exchange for friendship, which is more than Parim has offered in a generation.

honorary_crowns.title: An Honour from Parim
honorary_crowns.desc: A herald in the King's livery presents a crown of gilded iron and a scroll naming this realm an honorary member of the Lost Cause. It is a gift of ribbons and ceremony, and it carries the King's friendship.

league_triumph.title: A Triumph for the League
league_triumph.desc: Knights in gilt mail wind through the capital beneath the banners of the Lost Cause. The people throw flowers, the heralds shout the old oaths, and the treasury quietly pays for all of it.

rangers_of_selen.title: The Rangers Answer
rangers_of_selen.desc: The King's letter asks Selen to lend its rangers to the Lost Cause. The captains of Selen read it aloud in the green hall, and the room is divided between pride and suspicion.

black_ships.title: The Black Ships
black_ships.desc: Fishermen on the western coast tell of black hulls that move without wind and show lanterns of the wrong colour. The harbour-master wants to know whether the King's court will listen.

options.name: Send a ship north to look.

southern_warnings.title: Warnings from the South
southern_warnings.desc: In 4A 1736 an envoy from Mirolon came to Parim with a warning about the Ember Lands, and the court laughed. The archive still holds his letters, and someone has begun to read them.

options.name: Laugh, as the court did before.

hidden_hand.title: The Hidden Hand
hidden_hand.desc: In the long evenings the King's clerks lay the rolls of appointments side by side. Whoever filled the great offices of the realm did so with a patience and a purpose no courtier ever showed. It is hard to say whose hand it is, and harder to stop asking.

options.name: Mark the pattern, and say nothing.

deliverer_feast.title: The Feast of the Deliverer
deliverer_feast.desc: On the longest night every hearth in Aenor lights a white candle, and the temple halls serve bread to all who come. In the great hall of the Houses of the First Light the choir sings until dawn.

ledger_of_heirs.title: The Ledger of Heirs
ledger_of_heirs.desc: For thirty days the throne has been empty. The Regency's clerks open the great rolls and read out the names of the royal house, and the court argues over who may be named and who may be safely forgotten.

options.name: Search the old rolls for an heir.

eastern_friends.title: Gifts from Parim
eastern_friends.desc: A new king in Aenor sends his greeting across the rift sea: caskets of gold, bolts of white cloth and a letter that asks for nothing. The court of the East turns the letter over and over.

men_of_selen.title: The Men of Selen
men_of_selen.desc: The rangers have heard the Hailed King speak, and they are of one mind. The captains ask only whether Selen marches now or after the border is safe.

southern_aid.title: Aid from Aenor
southern_aid.desc: A column of Aenoran wagons halts at the Mirolon passes, bearing spears and shields from the arsenals of Parim. The captain says only that the court has remembered a warning it once laughed at.

league_invite.title: The League of Free Crowns
league_invite.desc: The Speakers of the Concord of Equals write to your court. Aenor has no wish to rule beyond its borders, but it asks you to stand beside it against the powers of the dark.

treaties.title: Treaties, Not Conquest
treaties.desc: A herald in the new king's colours stands at your gate. The King of Aenor offers peace on equal terms, with no tribute asked and no land taken.

fourth_age_ends.title: The Fourth Age Ends
fourth_age_ends.desc: The bells of Parim ring for three days. A king has been crowned among the ruins, and the heralds cry that the Fourth Age is over. He wears a necklace of black stone about his throat, which the chroniclers describe and do not explain. What it costs him is not known.

free_peoples.title: The Free Peoples Are Called
free_peoples.desc: A beacon burns on the hill and a rider stands at the gate. The Hailed King of Aenor asks every realm that fights the dark to stand under one banner.

common_cause_offer.title: A Common Cause
common_cause_offer.desc: Aenor sends word that the roads of its realm are open to every host that fights the dark, and asks that the roads of yours be open in return.

focuses.name: The Golden Court
focuses.desc: Seventeen centuries of the crown have gilded Parim until its halls outshine the lake. The King holds court at the water's edge, and every petitioner pays for the privilege of being heard.

focuses.name: The Sale of Offices
focuses.desc: Seals, tolls and captaincies go to whoever bids highest. The treasury fills at once, and the honest begin to leave the court.

focuses.name: Audit the Royal Treasury
focuses.desc: Clerks who owe nothing to the throne are set to count what the King's friends have taken. The sum will be a shock to somebody.

focuses.name: Gild the Halls of Parim
focuses.desc: Gold leaf for the pillars, silver for the stair-rails, mirrors for the vaults. The city shines and the court is pleased, and its debts grow with the glitter.

focuses.name: The Merchant Princes
focuses.desc: The great houses of the Lake pay handsomely for their charters, and the King lets them write the tariffs in return. Wealth follows, and so do favours.

focuses.name: Honest Ledgers
focuses.desc: Every purse that passes the treasury door is written in a book that any lord may read. The court grumbles; the tax-gatherers sleep better.

focuses.name: Dismiss the Flatterers
focuses.desc: The courtiers who echo the King's every word are sent back to their estates. The council chamber falls quiet, and for the first time in years someone says no.

focuses.name: A Royal Triumph
focuses.desc: Banners, drums and a procession from the lake gate to the palace steps. The crowds cheer a king whose battles are always won by someone else.

focuses.name: The Golden Tribute
focuses.desc: Heralds ride out to name the sum each dominion owes the throne. The coffers swell; the lords pay, and remember.

focuses.name: The Royal Mint
focuses.desc: New dies, true weights and an assay no clerk can bribe. Coin from Parim rings clear in every market again.

focuses.name: The Court of Accounts
focuses.desc: A standing bench of auditors may summon any officer of the realm to answer for a missing sum. Theft becomes a risk instead of a custom.

focuses.name: The Crown's Purse
focuses.desc: However the court has managed its gold, the treasury now answers to one purse and one seal. The King spends as he pleases, and knows to the coin what he has.

focuses.name: The Golden Jubilee
focuses.desc: Fifty days of feasting honour the long reign. Bells ring in every dominion, and nobody counts the cost until the lamps burn down.

focuses.name: Reform the Court
focuses.desc: Gilded fittings are sold, sinecures struck from the rolls and the court's hours given back to the kingdom's business. Those it used to feed will not forgive it.

focuses.name: The Great Lake Ports
focuses.desc: The Lake is Aenor's road and its larder. New quays, chain-booms and harbour-lights make its ports the busiest water in the Middle Lands.

focuses.name: The Roads of Parim
focuses.desc: Paved ways run from the palace gate to every dominion that owes the crown a tithe. Wagons that took a fortnight now take a week.

focuses.name: Lake Shipwrights
focuses.desc: Yards along the shore lay keels for broad, shallow ships that no sea captain would trust and no lake captain would be without.

focuses.name: Market Charters
focuses.desc: The King grants a fair to every town that asks, and takes a tenth of what is sold. More towns ask than anyone expected.

focuses.name: The Canal Works
focuses.desc: Gangs of diggers cut waterways between the lake and the rivers beyond it, and lock-keepers learn a trade that did not exist a generation ago.

focuses.name: The Lake Fleet
focuses.desc: A fleet of galleys keeps the lake lanes clear of smugglers and the shores clear of rumour. Its captains are proud and expensive.

focuses.name: Trade Across the Sea
focuses.desc: Aenoran cogs carry lake grain and Parim cloth out to the central sea, and come back with spice, glass and gossip from lands the court has never seen.

focuses.name: The Royal Foundries
focuses.desc: Furnaces ring the lake-towns, smelting iron for plough, nail and blade. The smoke is thick, and the King's smiths are paid in full.

focuses.name: The Guild Halls
focuses.desc: Each craft builds its own hall of carved timber and keeps its own rolls of masters. Apprentices travel from far shores to be bound there.

focuses.name: The Eastern Caravans
focuses.desc: Camel caravans from the far side of the rift sea reach Parim by the salt roads, and the court sends envoys with gifts to greet the caravan masters.

focuses.name: The Arsenals of Parim
focuses.desc: Armourers, fletchers and spear-makers work in vaulted halls beneath the palace hill, and the racks never stand empty.

focuses.name: The Universities of Parim and Selen
focuses.desc: The old halls of learning are endowed anew. Scholars of Parim and Selen share their books, and their quarrels, across the whole Middle Kingdom.

focuses.name: A Kingdom of Plenty
focuses.desc: Granaries are full, the roads are busy and the guilds are fat. For a season it seems that nothing in Aenor could ever go wrong.

focuses.name: The Kingdom's Armouries
focuses.desc: When the crown calls its banners, the armouries are thrown open and every smith in the realm turns to the forge.

focuses.name: The Middle Kingdom Concord
focuses.desc: Aenor and her twenty-six chartered dominions are one realm in law and many in custom. The Charters of Parim bind them; the King's heralds remind them.

focuses.name: Convene the Concord Council
focuses.desc: Lords of every dominion take their seats in the long hall at Parim, as their fathers did. They come to be heard, and the King comes to be obeyed.

focuses.name: Royal Envoys to the Dominions
focuses.desc: Heralds with the King's seal travel to every dominion court, and return with the true measure of each lord's loyalty written in a sealed roll.

focuses.name: The Golden Charters
focuses.desc: Privileges are sold to the dominion lords: tolls, mills and the right to hold their own courts. The Concord grows rich, and loyalty is for sale to the highest bidder.

focuses.name: The Charters of Parim Renewed
focuses.desc: The old charters are read aloud and sealed afresh. Every dominion is promised its liberties in plain words, and the lords weigh the promise against the King's record.

focuses.name: The Wall Charter
focuses.desc: Kingson, who keeps the gate in the Great Wall, is granted a charter of its own: freedom from tolls in return for an unbroken watch.

focuses.name: The Concord Levies
focuses.desc: Each dominion owes the crown a fixed muster of spears every year. The lords mutter, and the rolls are kept in Parim.

focuses.name: An Accord with Selen
focuses.desc: Selen's rangers hold the frontier and owe Parim little love. A written accord, signed in the green hall of Selen, offers them honour in place of orders.

focuses.name: The Isle of Asgard
focuses.desc: Off the western coast lies the isle of Asgard, whose houses have sworn to the crown since the first charter. A beacon-tower is raised on their headland.

focuses.name: The Gate of Kingson
focuses.desc: The gate in the Great Wall is rebuilt in dressed stone, with towers on either side and a portcullis that three men can raise.

focuses.name: The Tribute Roads
focuses.desc: Tribute wagons rumble towards Parim on new causeways, and the dominions learn exactly how far the King's hand can reach.

focuses.name: The Peoples of the Concord
focuses.desc: Kilinti's ents, the giants of Hiloron and the riders of Hunhun are invited to Parim as guests, not subjects. Their long memory is worth more than tribute.

focuses.name: The Common Army of the Concord
focuses.desc: Drill-masters of Parim teach the same signals, the same formations and the same marching songs to levies from every dominion.

focuses.name: The Concord Reborn
focuses.desc: The old compact is spoken again at the Council, and this time the lords mean the words. The Middle Kingdom stands as one realm, and says so.

focuses.name: The Oaths of the Lost Cause
focuses.desc: The King's league against the powers of the dark was sworn in 4A 1741, on the steps of the palace. Now its oaths are renewed before the lords of the realm, and nobody laughs.

focuses.name: The King's League
focuses.desc: Banners of the Lost Cause are raised above the palace court. It is a league of fine robes and grand words, and the King is its most devoted member.

focuses.name: The Frontier Companies
focuses.desc: Rangers, scouts and ex-soldiers are given the King's coin and sent to watch the borders where the maps run out. Few of them are in it for the banners.

focuses.name: The Scholars of the Cause
focuses.desc: Loremasters at Parim and Selen are paid to search the old records for whatever the dark powers did before, and how they were stopped.

focuses.name: A Triumph for the League
focuses.desc: A procession of knights in gilt mail winds through the capital to honour the Lost Cause. The people throw flowers, and the ledgers throw up a sum.

focuses.name: Honorary Crowns
focuses.desc: Far courts are offered a place in the league as honorary members. It costs the King only a few ribbons, and it may buy a friend who matters.

focuses.name: The Rangers of Selen
focuses.desc: The rangers of Selen are asked to lend their skills to the Lost Cause. They answer that the wild does not take orders, and then they come anyway.

focuses.name: Watchers on the Wall
focuses.desc: Beacon-keepers are posted every league along the Great Wall, with signal fires laid and ready. They watch the east and the south and pray to see nothing.

focuses.name: The Old Genealogies
focuses.desc: Heralds copy out the great houses' lines of descent, back to the First Men and the first charters. Old claims are found, and some old names are forgotten for good reason.

focuses.name: The Black Ships
focuses.desc: Fishermen on the western coast tell of black hulls moving without wind, and of lanterns that burn the wrong colour. The King's men note the tales and decide what to do.

focuses.name: Heed the Southern Warnings
focuses.desc: Mirolon's envoy brought word of the Ember Lands in 4A 1736 and was laughed out of the hall. Perhaps the archive still holds his letters.

focuses.name: The King's Tasters
focuses.desc: Every dish that reaches the King's table is first sampled by a trusted servant. The cooks are nervous, the King is amused and the physicians are quietly relieved.

focuses.name: The Shield of the Concord
focuses.desc: The Lost Cause stops being an ornament. Companies in the field, stores on the frontier and a charter of shields for every dominion that will take one.

focuses.name: The Hidden Hand
focuses.desc: Appointments to the great offices follow a pattern that no king set. Whoever is drawing it knows the court better than the King does.

focuses.name: Proof of Blood
focuses.desc: A man from the frontier carries a line of descent that the heralds cannot fault. Whoever stands behind him will want his claim made plain.

focuses.name: The Lost Cause Reborn
focuses.desc: The league is no longer the King's plaything. Its banners follow a stranger, and its companies at last fight for something they believe in.

focuses.name: The Temples of the Deliverer
focuses.desc: In every town of the Middle Kingdom the white-stoned temples of the Deliverer give bread, medicine and counsel. The King favours them; his people love them.

focuses.name: The Houses of the First Light
focuses.desc: Hospitals, grain stores and birth rolls, kept by the temples and open to all. No one in Aenor remembers when the realm did without them.

focuses.name: The Temple Schools
focuses.desc: Children of every rank learn their letters under the temple roofs. The teachers are kind, patient and thoroughly sure of what a child should believe.

focuses.name: The Keeper's Seals
focuses.desc: Merovan, who holds the seals of the realm, is given a hall of his own beside the throne room. Letters of state now reach the King by way of his table.

effects.tooltip: Merovan, Keeper of the Seals, gains authority in the King's council.

focuses.name: The Royal Almoners
focuses.desc: Almoners with the temples' badge walk the poorer quarters of Parim each dawn, and the poor bless a crown that seems to care.

focuses.name: The Birth Rolls
focuses.desc: The temples record every birth and every death in the realm, and the King's officers learn at last how many hands he can call to his banner.

focuses.name: The Blessed Crown
focuses.desc: The King is anointed in the great temple, and the Deliverer's priests proclaim him favoured of heaven. The people kneel more readily afterwards.

focuses.name: The King's Own Counsel
focuses.desc: The King reminds his councillors that he alone appoints them. The temples bow, smile and remain exactly where they were.

focuses.name: The Feast of the Deliverer
focuses.desc: On the longest night every hearth in Aenor lights a white candle, and every temple hall serves bread to all who come. The Deliverer's blessing is spoken in the King's name.

focuses.name: One Faith, One Realm
focuses.desc: The King decrees that the Deliverer's rites shall be kept in every dominion. The temples are glad, the Concord is quiet, and a few old shrines go dark.

focuses.name: The Royal Army of Aenor
focuses.desc: The King's host is the strongest in the Middle Lands, and he keeps it sharp. It parades at every feast and has not yet been asked to fight.

focuses.name: Commissions for Sale
focuses.desc: Captaincies go to the sons of men who can afford them. The ranks are filled with polished boots and unpractised spears.

focuses.name: Commissions by Merit
focuses.desc: Officers are chosen by trial and by record, not by purse. Some noble houses are insulted, and the soldiers cheer.

focuses.name: The Great Wall of Aenor
focuses.desc: From the Organ Mountains to the gate at Kingson the Wall stands, as it has since the Wall Accord. Its towers are repaired and its ditches dug afresh.

focuses.name: The Golden Guard
focuses.desc: Two thousand picked men in gilded helms are quartered in the palace barracks. They cost a fortune, and they look splendid at the gate.

focuses.name: The Drill Fields
focuses.desc: Wide meadows beside the lake are cleared for the daily drill. Veterans teach shield-wall and volley to recruits who thought a march was a stroll.

focuses.name: Garrisons of the Wall
focuses.desc: Companies are quartered in the towers along the Wall, and relieved each season. Kingson's lords send wine for the watch.

focuses.name: Watch on the Coasts
focuses.desc: Look-out towers rise on every headland of the western shore, and fishermen are paid to count the sails they see.

focuses.name: Pacify the Bloody Forest
focuses.desc: The Bloody Forest has never accepted the crown, and its raiders have never stopped trying the borders of the Concord. The Golden Guard is sent to teach it manners.

focuses.name: A New Doctrine of War
focuses.desc: Marshals of the old school argue with young captains over the lessons of the frontier. The King listens to both and decides for neither, so both are heard.

focuses.name: Fortresses on the Strait
focuses.desc: The narrow waters between Aenor and the Dark Lands are lined with stone keeps, each with its own chain, harbour and fire-pit.

focuses.name: The King's Host
focuses.desc: When the King raises his standard, the Host answers: heavy foot, horse and archers in the colours of the lake. It will be a sight to see, and a worse one to face.

focuses.name: Mobilise the Realm
focuses.desc: Beacons burn from the Wall to the lake, and every dominion is bidden to send its men. Aenor goes to war as it has not in generations.

focuses.name: Poison in the Cup
focuses.desc: A taster falls ill on a cup meant for the King. The court whispers of poison, and for the first time in years the King listens to a voice other than his own.

focuses.name: Arrest the Keeper of Seals
focuses.desc: Merovan is taken from his hall at dawn, still wearing the chain of his office. The seals pass back into the King's own hand, and the Council's friends at court lose their voice.

effects.tooltip: Merovan, Keeper of the Seals, is removed from the King's council.

focuses.name: Seize the Houses' Ledgers
focuses.desc: Royal officers enter the Houses of the First Light and carry off every roll and tally. The temples protest, loudly, and the ledgers are read aloud in open court.

focuses.name: The Loyal Clergy
focuses.desc: Priests who served the crown before the Deliverer's temples filled the city are brought back to the great altar. They preach obedience to the King, and the people hear them out.

focuses.name: The King's War
focuses.desc: The Council's friends have taken up arms. The King, sobered and furious, rides out at the head of his Host.

focuses.name: The Golden King Reborn
focuses.desc: The man who sold his offices is gone. In his place sits a king who has looked at his own death and learned what it is worth.

focuses.name: The Regency of Gold
focuses.desc: The throne stands empty and the Golden Court rules in its name. The seals are kept in a gilded casket, and every decree begins with the words "For the crown".

focuses.name: Buy the Captains
focuses.desc: Every captain of the Host receives a purse and a promise. Most of them take both.

focuses.name: The Ledger of Heirs
focuses.desc: Heralds open the great rolls and read the names of the royal house aloud. The Regency must find a name to rule for, and few are free of suspicion.

focuses.name: A Golden Peace
focuses.desc: Envoys carry gold to Lerendor and Gunwaith with the offer of a long truce. They return richer in promises than in friends.

focuses.name: Crush the Pretenders
focuses.desc: Every rival camp is named an enemy of the crown. Captains with warrants ride to arrest their leaders before the next feast.

focuses.name: Gold for the Dominions
focuses.desc: The treasury opens to the dominion lords one last time. Those who take the coin swear to the Regency; those who refuse are remembered.

focuses.name: The Treasury of War
focuses.desc: The Regency pours its hoard into forges and storehouses. The gold of seventeen centuries becomes spears.

focuses.name: A Crown Kept for No King
focuses.desc: The crown rests on its cushion in the empty throne room, and the Regency rules in its shadow. No king has been named, and the Golden Court means to keep it so.

focuses.name: First of His Name
focuses.desc: The Deliverer takes the crown of Aenor in the great temple of Parim, under the name of Aurevan, and the bells ring for three days. Old men weep at the gates; children are lifted to see him pass.

focuses.name: The Seals of State
focuses.desc: A new chancery is founded in the palace, with scribes in white and seals of silver. Every decree of the realm now passes beneath the Deliverer's eye.

focuses.name: Silence the Dissenters
focuses.desc: Lords and captains who question the new reign are called to the temple and spoken to kindly. Most of them stop questioning.

focuses.name: Temple and Crown
focuses.desc: Altar and throne are joined: the temples sit in the council, and the crown shelters the temples. Few remember a time it was otherwise.

focuses.name: The Deliverer's Relief
focuses.desc: Grain wagons roll from the Houses of the First Light to every hungry dominion. The people name the new king their saviour, and they mean it.

focuses.name: Friends in the East
focuses.desc: Gifts and letters go to the courts of Noris, Stabilo and Alerhia, with the Deliverer's blessing and no demands attached. The gifts are generous.

focuses.name: Denounce the Impostor
focuses.desc: A man from the frontier is hailed by common folk as the rightful heir. The Deliverer's heralds declare him a fraud, and the temples ring with the denunciation.

focuses.name: The Shield of Deliverance
focuses.desc: Wards are carved above the gates of Parim, and the temple guard is posted in every tower. The Deliverer's city will not be taken.

focuses.name: The Oaths of the Realm
focuses.desc: Every lord, captain and magistrate kneels in the temple to swear fealty to the Deliverer's crown. The oaths are written in a book that is kept under lock.

focuses.name: Hold Parim for the Crown
focuses.desc: The war has come to the lake. Every gate of the capital is walled, every tower manned and every bell readied to ring when the enemy is seen.

focuses.name: The Concord of Equals
focuses.desc: The Free Dominions take the seals of Aenor and declare the Charters of Parim a compact among equals. The crown is a chair at the table, no more.

focuses.name: The Speakers' Council
focuses.desc: Each dominion sends a speaker with a single voice. The council meets in the open hall and votes by raised hands, and the loudest do not always win.

focuses.name: Letters to the Free Dominions
focuses.desc: Messengers carry an offer to each dominion that left the Concord: return under a Free Charter, or stay free and be a friend.

focuses.name: A Common Defence
focuses.desc: Dominions pledge spears to a shared host under a marshal chosen by the Speakers. Each keeps its own banner and its own captains.

focuses.name: Equal Tolls
focuses.desc: Customs on every road and river are set at one rate, the same for Parim and the smallest dominion. Merchants praise it; old tollkeepers do not.

focuses.name: Restore the Charters by Force
focuses.desc: Those who left the Concord will be brought back by the Speakers' orders, and by the Host if need be. The Charters, after all, are law.

focuses.name: The League of Free Crowns
focuses.desc: Letters go to Mirolon, Lerendor and Gunwaith. The Concord of Equals has no ambitions beyond its borders, and wishes its neighbours to know it.

focuses.name: The Concord Stands
focuses.desc: The old compact has been remade by consent, and it is stronger for it. Aenor and its dominions keep their charters, their quarrels and their peace.

focuses.name: The King Without a House
focuses.desc: He has no palace, no treasury and no crown, only a following of rangers, scholars and plain folk who believe he is their king. They call him the Hailed King.

focuses.name: The Hailed King's Claim
focuses.desc: The line of Aen did not end with the Golden Court. The heralds have found the proof, and a stranger from the frontier carries it in his blood.

focuses.name: The Men of Selen
focuses.desc: The rangers of Selen ride beneath the Hailed King's banner. Selen has waited a long time for a king who deserved it.

focuses.name: Call the Free Peoples
focuses.desc: Beacons are lit on the highest hills, and messengers go to every realm that fights the dark. The King Without a House asks only for their spears.

focuses.name: The Light of Glo
focuses.desc: A green light burns in the Hailed King's hand. Men who see it grow quiet, and the dark things that watch the host draw back.

focuses.name: No Crown Taken by Force
focuses.desc: The King Without a House will not take any dominion's loyalty at sword-point. Charters are offered freely, and the dominions are asked to come as friends.

focuses.name: The Last Alliance of Men
focuses.desc: Banners of the Middle Lands, the Cold Lands and the western clans stand together under the Hailed King. It is the largest muster of men since the Grand Alliance.

focuses.name: The Dragon Banner
focuses.desc: A dragon wheels above the Hailed King's host, and no horse in Aoaz will stand against it. Men who laughed at the old tales stop laughing.

focuses.name: Retake Parim
focuses.desc: The capital lies in the hands of the western host. The King Without a House marches to take it back, street by street if he must.

focuses.name: The People Choose Their King
focuses.desc: In the ruins of the lake gate the people raise their hands. They ask for the Hailed King, and he, at last, says yes.

focuses.name: The Abandoned Throne
focuses.desc: The Deliverer has gone and taken his guards with him. The throne room is silent, the temples are shuttered and the realm must remember how to rule itself.

focuses.name: The Captains' Rule
focuses.desc: The captains of the Host take the keys of the capital. They have never ruled before, and they intend to do it briefly.

focuses.name: Open the Temple Vaults
focuses.desc: The temples' treasuries are broken open and counted. The gold goes to arms, the grain to the hungry and the ledgers to the archives.

focuses.name: Send for the Stranger
focuses.desc: The captains have heard of a man from the frontier whom the common folk hail as their king. They send riders to find him and ask him to come.

focuses.name: Aenor Beset
focuses.desc: Enemies press from every side, and the Middle Kingdom must hold. Every dominion is asked to remember what it owes the crown.

focuses.name: Hold the Western Shore
focuses.desc: The coast is lined with new forts, all facing the sea. Fishermen are paid to watch, and signal-masters are posted on every headland.

focuses.name: The Strait Betrayed
focuses.desc: The north shore is no longer a friend. Lerendor has left the old treaty, and the narrow waters must be guarded as a frontier.

focuses.name: Against the Deathless Dead
focuses.desc: The dead walk out of the north at Zol's will. Ordinary weapons break them but cannot end them, and the Host must learn to hold the line whatever the cost.

effects.tooltip: Ordinary weapons break Zol's dead but cannot end them.

focuses.name: The Wall Holds
focuses.desc: From the Organ Mountains to Kingson the watchfires burn. The Wall has been breached before, and every man on it knows the story.

focuses.name: The Southern Front
focuses.desc: Companies from the southern marches rally at Mirolon's passes. The Ember Lands are no longer a rumour but a border.

focuses.name: The Levy of the Lake
focuses.desc: Every village on the lake is told to send one man in three. They come, and the barracks of the capital overflow.

focuses.name: Fortress Parim
focuses.desc: The palace hill is ringed in stone, the lake gate chained, the cisterns filled. Parim has not known a siege in seventeen centuries.

focuses.name: A Common Cause
focuses.desc: Riders go to every realm that fights the dark powers. Aenor asks for open roads and offers its own in return.

focuses.name: The Last Stand of the Middle Kingdom
focuses.desc: If the Middle Kingdom falls, it will fall at Parim. Every soldier, mason and baker takes a post, and the lake gate is sealed.

focuses.name: A Kingdom of Ruins
focuses.desc: The war is over, and what is left of Aenor must be built anew. The King walks among broken walls and orders them raised, stone by stone.

focuses.name: Treaties, Not Conquest
focuses.desc: Heralds ride to every realm still at war with Aenor with the same offer: peace now, on equal terms. The King wants no more enemies.

focuses.name: The Fourth Age Ends
focuses.desc: A king crowned among ruins, a realm that must learn to live in peace. The chroniclers will write that the Fourth Age ended here, and will not yet know what it cost.
